blocking_findings.summary: The optional Sentry and LangSmith exporters are triple-gated but are not payload-safe after opt-in.
evidence: core/observability.py enables LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2 globally when the three LangSmith gates pass.

agents/manager_agent.py has seven active @traceable Manager graph nodes at lines 948, 969, 1010, 1028, 1076, 1133 and 1254 without process_inputs/process_outputs allowlists; their g argument and returned dictionaries contain Shared State, task query, preferences, reasoning, evidence and result payloads.

core/error_handler.py:68 sends the original exception object with sentry_sdk.capture_exception(exc), and the request Manager path calls capture_exception on original exceptions at agents/manager_agent.py:424, 561, 764, 868, 1200, 1246 and 1274.

The Stage 10A local lifecycle helper is allowlisted, but init_langsmith/init_sentry activate these separate pre-existing export paths. Therefore PRIVATE_SENTINEL coverage limited to the local sink and initializer failures does not prove exporter payload safety, and OBS-10A-002/003 are not fully resolved.
blocking_findings.contract_violation: The Stage 10A contract and CR1 require optional exporters to remain payload-safe and forbid raw query, user/preferences, Manager/Shared State, exception objects/text/stacks, reasoning and raw evidence from export.

blocking_findings.summary: The user-authorized analyze route exception exceeded its privacy/observability-only scope.
evidence: The draft-ready artifact did not include api/routes/analyze.py; the later user authorization and ENTER_PRIMARY_FINAL transition limited this path to privacy/observability call-sites with business_contract_change=false.

The route diff imports get_request_manager and replaces request.app.state.manager_agent with get_request_manager(request, memory). This changes runtime Manager resolution and request binding, not a logging, telemetry or redaction call-site.
The route diff also adds a new persistence-status normalization branch. This is outside the authorized privacy/observability correction even if current known statuses make it normally inert.
The implementation and QA artifacts state that analyze business routing/Manager behavior is unchanged, which is contradicted by the recorded diff.
blocking_findings.contract_violation: Every changed path must stay within the exact lock authorization. Stage 10B route behavior remained unauthorized, and the narrow route exception did not authorize Manager resolution or status-flow edits.

non_blocking_findings.summary: The optional seed.command.selected event was not added.
non_blocking_findings.assessment: This remains honest and non-blocking because normal serve/default startup never seeds and seed-rag remains the only explicit seed command.

scope_violations.assessment: The path had a valid exact lock, but get_request_manager(request, memory) and the new status normalization exceeded the user-authorized privacy/observability-only purpose of that lock.

required_rework.required: Keep external exporters disabled until every request-reachable trace/capture path is payload-safe, or perform an explicitly locked audit and repair of all such paths. LangSmith traces must use closed process_inputs/process_outputs allowlists and Sentry must never capture original exception objects or request-derived scalar payloads. Add offline enabled-exporter PRIVATE_SENTINEL countertests proving Manager node inputs/outputs, exceptions, logs and breadcrumbs contain only compact allowlisted metadata and that exporter/client failures remain non-fatal.

Either revert the analyze route Manager-resolution and status-normalization edits while retaining the authorized privacy/observability sanitation, or obtain explicit authorization for those exact behavior changes and revalidate them in a new attempt. The next implementation and QA artifacts must describe the route diff accurately.

resolved_findings.evidence: Local API startup/shutdown/request and request-scoped Manager/memory events use immutable 10A/r1/a1/core identity, one opaque UUID4-hex request id, measured finite non-negative latency, a closed local metadata allowlist and isolated sink failure.

The changed API route and memory logs/persistence remove raw request and exception values, but enabled Sentry still receives original exceptions from request-reachable Manager paths and enabled LangSmith can trace raw Manager graph state.
All three activation gates and non-fatal initializer handling are present, but successful activation exposes separate non-allowlisted exporter call-sites, so payload safety is not established.
